reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / WHO / India national programmes
clinicalPearls: A highly lethal zoonotic paramyxovirus (henipavirus) whose natural reservoir is fruit bats (Pteropus species)

In India transmission has been linked to consumption of date-palm sap contaminated by bat secretions and to close contact with infected patients, with documented person-to-person and nosocomial spread
Presents as rapidly progressive encephalitis with fever, headache, altered mental status and often prominent brainstem signs; respiratory involvement may also occur
Case fatality is very high, and survivors may suffer residual neurological deficits or relapsing/late-onset encephalitis
No licensed antiviral or vaccine is established; management is supportive with rigorous infection control
Strict barrier precautions, patient isolation and contact tracing are essential because human-to-human transmission drives outbreaks
It is classified as a priority pathogen of pandemic potential requiring immediate public-health notification
Diagnosis uses RT-PCR on respiratory secretions, CSF, urine or blood, and serology (IgM/IgG ELISA), performed in high-containment laboratories
reference.pathophysiology: Nipah virus is an enveloped RNA henipavirus that infects endothelium and neurons. After spillover from fruit bats (directly, via contaminated food, or from intermediate hosts such as pigs), the virus causes a systemic vasculitis with endothelial infection, syncytium formation, thrombosis and microinfarction, particularly in the central nervous system. This vasculitic and direct neuronal injury produces the severe encephalitis, while pulmonary endothelial and epithelial infection can cause acute respiratory distress. The capacity of the virus to persist may underlie relapsing or delayed-onset encephalitis in some survivors.
additionalDifferentials: Japanese encephalitis and other viral encephalitides
additionalInvestigations: RT-PCR of throat/nasal swabs, CSF, urine and blood in a biosafe reference laboratory
Nipah-specific IgM and IgG serology by ELISA
MRI brain, which may show disseminated small cortical and subcortical lesions
CSF examination when safe, typically showing lymphocytic pleocytosis
Chest imaging if respiratory involvement is suspected
redFlags: Rapidly deteriorating consciousness or brainstem dysfunction signalling life-threatening encephalitis
Any respiratory distress raising concern for airborne/droplet transmissibility and severe disease
Cluster of cases or contact with a confirmed case, mandating immediate isolation and outbreak response
Autonomic instability or seizures requiring critical-care support
reference.prognosis: Nipah virus disease is one of the most lethal human encephalitides, with case fatality frequently exceeding half of symptomatic cases. Survivors may be left with persistent neurological impairment, and a minority develop relapsing or late-onset encephalitis months to years later.
pitfalls: Failing to institute isolation and barrier precautions early, allowing nosocomial and family transmission
Delaying notification to public-health authorities during a suspected cluster
Attributing the illness to more common encephalitides and not sending appropriate high-containment testing
Underestimating the risk to healthcare workers during aerosol-generating procedures
management: Deliver intensive supportive care as there is no licensed antiviral, with mechanical ventilation and organ support for encephalitis and acute respiratory distress
Consider investigational therapies such as ribavirin or a monoclonal antibody (m102.4) within research or compassionate-use frameworks
Enforce strict infection control with patient isolation, barrier precautions and personal protective equipment, given documented person-to-person and nosocomial transmission
Manage the encephalitis with seizure control, treatment of raised intracranial pressure and meticulous neurocritical care
Notify public health authorities and undertake contact tracing and outbreak control, including avoidance of raw date-palm sap and contact with sick animals
Monitor survivors for residual neurological deficits and for relapsing or late-onset encephalitis
Coordinate care through infectious diseases and critical care within a designated high-consequence pathogen pathway
